text: Whenever you take it easy, you take people with you. Your first try already looks right, and they see the ease without the care behind it. You teach them to aim no higher than what you settle for.

findings.issue: Round 1's X-07 is still open. The reader is the exacting one and the one who settles, on the same page.
findings.auditor_note: Chip "Makes it look easy". "Whenever you make it look easy, the people learning from you see only the finish. Your first try already looks right, and the checking behind it stays hidden. You leave them aiming at an ease they never watched you earn."

findings.issue: The same page's drive says "A thing has to be right in every detail before it pleases you". The reader is a perfectionist and someone who settles on one page. The passage itself says there is care behind the ease and then says the reader settles. (Round 1 MT-24; the M5 rewrite softened it but kept "settle".)
findings.auditor_note: "Whenever you take it easy, you take people with you. Your skill makes hard work look light, and those near you copy the ease without the care behind it. You pass on the ease and leave them without the craft." (40)

text: Whenever something comes to you without effort, you count it as worth less. Trusting the forced version more than the easy one, you add effort to finished work. Your evenings disappear into polishing what was right the first time.

findings.issue: The chip says ease and the passage says perfectionism. The Artisan is a coaster on its own Water friction page (P139: "Drifting is easier than steering"). On the blend P144 it sits beside the Virtuoso's "Getting the laugh with the quick line", a second slow-versus-quick pull on one page.
findings.auditor_note: "Unforced is the only way you work. Since effort that shows feels like trying too hard, you stop at the easy version rather than push it further. You leave some of your best ideas as sketches a second pass would have made great."

findings.issue: This is the Virtuoso's cost ("you redo finished work. You spend whole weekends changing things that were already good enough", 水_伤官 cat[1]). It is also out of character for the Artisan, who on the friction pole of the same cell puts "comfort first" and drifts. The Artisan's own price is undervaluing what comes easily.
findings.auditor_note: "Whenever something comes to you without effort, you count it as worth less. You trust the forced version more than the easy one, and the easy one stays in the drawer. You price lowest the things you do best." (40)

text: Picking the moment keeps you from wasting yourself. You hold your force for the turn that matters, and the smaller openings pass while you watch for it. Some of your best chances go to people quicker off the mark.

findings.issue: Round 1's X-08 is only half fixed. The General still loses to quicker people, against its own drive on the same page ("you want the next move more than the right feeling").
findings.auditor_note: "Picking the moment is where your nerve shows. You hold your force through the small openings and move the instant the turn that matters comes. You spend the quiet weeks on watch, and few see what that costs you."

text: For you, a good choice beats a fast one. Since getting the choice right matters more to you than being on time, you let the warm moment pass. Underneath it, you want to be known as someone who truly listens.

findings.issue: The want in the close does not follow from choosing well. It reads as a close pasted in from another passage.
findings.auditor_note: "For you, a good choice beats a fast one. Since getting the choice right matters more to you than being on time, you let the warm moment pass. You often bring the gift you chose with care after the occasion is over."

findings.issue: The close does not follow. Nothing in "Chooses well" is about listening. "the warm moment" has no referent.
findings.auditor_note: "For you, a good choice beats a fast one. Getting it right matters more to you than being on time, and the moment often passes while you weigh it. Underneath, you want to look back and still be glad of what you picked." (43)

text: Spending from the shared pot is the easiest money there is. More Water moves through you than you keep, so you pay for everyone's good time before your savings. You come out with the least from a pot you paid the most into.

findings.issue: It is "easy" money that is somehow also mostly your own, and the reason given is chart arithmetic (X2-03).
findings.auditor_note: "Spending from the shared pot feels like generosity. More of your own money goes into it than anyone else's, and you spend it on everyone's good time before your needs. You come out with the least from a pot you paid the most into."

findings.issue: Sentence 1 says you spend the shared money. Sentences 2 and 3 say you are the one paying into it. The chip and the drive angle (P147, "you dip into it before asking who put what in") both mean the first. The cause is also an amount of Water (W-002).
findings.auditor_note: "Spending from the shared pot is the easiest money there is. It never feels like yours, and the pot pays for your good times before your own savings do. You end up owing the group more than you noticed spending." (40)
